cues.en: Another thing Netflix says repeatedly, which we've also said repeatedly in this course, is to not focus on accurately predicting rating values.
cues.zh: Netflix 反覆強調另一件事，本課程也反覆說過，就是不要把焦點放在準確預測評分值。

cues.en: This is a little bit ironic, given that the focus on rating predictions was really driven by the Netflix Prize itself.
cues.zh: 這有點諷刺，因為大家重視評分預測，其實正是 Netflix Prize 推動的。

cues.en: Today however, Netflix has done away with star ratings entirely, so they couldn't train on them even if they wanted to.
cues.zh: 但如今 Netflix 已經完全取消星等評分，所以即使想用，也無法拿它來訓練。

cues.en: They talk about how they have evolved by initially focusing on rating prediction, to focusing on rankings instead, and finally to whole-page optimization.
cues.zh: 他們談到，最初著重評分預測，後來演進為關注排序，最後走向整頁最佳化。

cues.en: Although they don't call it out specifically, YouTube isn't trying to predict ratings either, they are optimizing on minutes watched, and their objective function is learned over time
cues.zh: 雖然沒有特別點出，YouTube 也不是要預測評分，而是最佳化觀看分鐘數；其目標函數是隨時間，

cues.en: from live A/B tests, not on any offline accuracy metric.
cues.zh: 從即時 A/B 測試學來的，而非根據任何離線準確度指標。

cues.en: Netflix also relies on live A/B tests online to tune its systems, they use what they call an offline-online testing procedure to use offline metrics to get an initial cut
cues.zh: Netflix 也依賴線上的即時 A/B 測試來調整系統。他們使用所謂離線到線上測試流程，先以離線指標初步篩選，

cues.en: at which new ideas might perform well online, and then use live online A/B tests to validate those ideas on real people.
cues.zh: 哪些新想法可能在線上表現良好，再用線上即時 A/B 測試，向真實使用者驗證。

cues.en: That's basically the approach we've promoted throughout this course.
cues.zh: 這基本上就是本課程一直提倡的方法。

cues.en: Netflix also notes that ratings data is inherently noisy, which limits the usefulness of RMSE as a metric for your recommender system.
cues.zh: Netflix 也指出，評分資料本來就有雜訊，限制了 RMSE 作為推薦系統指標的實用性。

cues.en: Remember YouTube abandoned the use of explicit ratings entirely, so it seems they both reached the same conclusion here.
cues.zh: 記得，YouTube 已完全放棄使用明確評分，所以看來兩者得到相同結論。

cues.en: Also similar to YouTube, Netflix has separated out the problems of candidate generation with ranking them, and has invested a lot in their own personalized learning-to-rank approach.
cues.zh: 同樣與 YouTube 類似，Netflix 把候選項目產生與排序問題分開，並大量投入自己的個人化學習排序方法。

cues.en: Learning-to-rank basically treats the problem of generating a top-N list as a classification problem, which each slot in the top N is a classification you are trying to learn.
cues.zh: 學習排序基本上把產生 Top-N 清單視為分類問題，Top-N 中每個位置，都是要學習的分類。

cues.en: Although they are cagey on the details of how they do this, again they name-drop a few examples of how you might do it, including RankSVM, RankBoost, RankNet, and BPR.
cues.zh: 雖然他們對做法細節守口如瓶，但又列出一些可能採用的方法，例如 RankSVM、RankBoost、RankNet 和 BPR。

cues.en: They don't just use the results of their personalized learning to rank system as-is, though.
cues.zh: 不過，他們不會原封不動地使用個人化學習排序系統的結果。

cues.en: They intentionally factor in the popularity of the results as well at the end, to try and balance predicted rankings with popularity.
cues.zh: 最後還會刻意納入結果的熱門度，嘗試平衡預測排名與熱門程度。

cues.en: As we've mentioned, showing some popular items is essential to producing user trust in the system, and getting them to engage with it.
cues.zh: 如前所述，顯示一些熱門項目，對建立使用者信任並讓他們願意互動很重要。

cues.en: As with YouTube, recommendation candidates come along with scores or rating predictions that you could just sort to get a top-N list, but they've taken this a step further
cues.zh: 和 YouTube 一樣，候選推薦帶有分數或預測評分，直接排序就能得到 Top-N 清單，但他們更進一步，

cues.en: and applied machine learning to finding the best order to present those final results in, incorporating more information than just those predicted ratings.
cues.zh: 應用機器學習，找出呈現最終結果的最佳順序，納入的不只是那些預測評分，還有更多資訊。

cues.en: Netflix, like YouTube, has found that the more features you train your system with, the better.
cues.zh: 和 YouTube 一樣，Netflix 發現訓練系統使用的特徵越多越好。

cues.en: It's not just about which videos you watched in the past, it's also about how you watched them.
cues.zh: 不只是過去看過哪些影片，也包括如何觀看。

cues.en: And the circumstances you're in right now might affect what sorts of content are best to show to you right now.
cues.zh: 你現在的情境，也可能影響此刻最適合顯示的內容。

cues.en: For example, are you likely to view different kinds of content depending on which device you're viewing it on?
cues.zh: 例如，你是否會因為觀看裝置不同，而偏好不同類型的內容？

cues.en: If you're accessing Netflix from your big screen TV, perhaps that's the device you use personally, and recommending longer-form content aimed at adults is what makes sense.
cues.zh: 若透過大螢幕電視使用 Netflix，也許那是你個人使用的裝置，推薦較長、以成人為對象的內容，就很合理。

cues.en: If your kid uses your Netflix account on a tablet, making recommendations based on what you've watched from that tablet would surface shorter, kid-focused content that makes sense in that context.
cues.zh: 若孩子在平板上使用你的 Netflix 帳號，根據在那台平板看過的內容推薦，就會呈現較短、適合兒童的內容，符合當下情境。

cues.en: The time might make a difference as well.
cues.zh: 時間也可能有影響。

cues.en: You might be open to more mature content late at night, than you would in the afternoon when the kids are around.
cues.zh: 比起孩子在身旁的下午，你在深夜可能更願意看成人向的內容。

cues.en: Even the day of the week might matter, you may be looking to kill more time on the weekends, and so you might prefer movies on weekends and TV shows during the week.
cues.zh: 甚至一週中的哪一天也可能有關。週末也許想打發較多時間，所以週末偏好電影，平日則偏好電視節目。

cues.en: These are all examples of the context in which you are seeking recommendations, and a good recommender system will use all of this information to refine the results it returns.
cues.zh: 這些都是你尋求推薦時的情境。好的推薦系統，會利用所有這些資訊，改進回傳結果。

cues.en: Those are the main points Netflix has shared with us, but they are insightful.
cues.zh: 以上是 Netflix 分享的主要重點，很有啟發性。

cues.en: It's also interesting that even though Netflix and YouTube are both in the business of recommending videos, they are doing so in slightly different settings and with slightly different requirements
cues.zh: 有趣的是，雖然 Netflix 與 YouTube 都在做影片推薦，但情境與需求稍有不同，

cues.en: that have informed their choices of algorithms and technology.
cues.zh: 因而影響了演算法與技術的選擇。
